ko.title: 헤드라인 대 코어: 다음 CPI 보고서를 읽는 법과 내 물가가 다르게 느껴지는 이유

segments.src: Once a month, usually at 8:30 a.m.
segments.tr: 한 달에 한 번, 보통 월요일에서 금요일 중 중순쯤의 동부 시간 기준으로

segments.src: Eastern on a weekday around the middle of the month, the U.S.
segments.tr: 오전 8시 30분경에 미국

segments.src: Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) publishes the Consumer Price Index (CPI).
segments.tr: 노동통계국(BLS)은 소비자물가지수(CPI)를 발표합니다.

segments.src: Within minutes, headlines announce whether inflation "cooled," "reheated," or "surprised."
segments.tr: 몇 분 안에 헤드라인 뉴스는 인플레이션이 "냉판해졌는지", "다시 올랐는지", 아니면 "예상을 뒤엎었는지"를 발표합니다.

segments.src: Yet many readers look at their own grocery receipts, rent, and gas bills and wonder why the official number doesn't match their experience.
segments.tr: 그러나 많은 독자들은 자신의 식료품 영수증, 임대료, 가스 요금을 보며 공식적인 수치가 왜 자신의 경험과 일치하지 않는지 의아해합니다.

segments.src: This guide explains what the CPI measures, how the headline and core readings differ, what each major category contributes, and why your personal inflation rate can differ from the national figure.
segments.tr: 이 가이드는 CPI가 측정하는 것, 헤드라인과 코어 물가 상승률의 차이점, 각 주요 카테고리가 기여하는 부분, 그리고 개인의 인플레이션율이 국가 수치와 다를 수 있는 이유를 설명합니다.

segments.src: It is educational background, not financial advice.
segments.tr: 이는 교육적 배경일 뿐 재정적 조언이 아닙니다.

segments.src: ## Why the CPI Matters
segments.tr: ## CPI가 중요한 이유

segments.src: The CPI tracks the average change over time in prices paid by urban consumers for a fixed basket of goods and services.
segments.tr: CPI는 도시 소비자가 고정된 상품 및 서비스 바구니에 대해 지불하는 가격의 시간에 따른 평균 변화를 추적합니다.

segments.src: It feeds into several things that touch daily life:
segments.tr: 이는 일상생활에 영향을 미치는 여러 요소에 반영됩니다:

segments.src: - **Interest-rate expectations.** The Federal Reserve targets 2% inflation, measured by a related gauge called the PCE price index. Markets still treat the CPI, which arrives earlier, as a key signal for where rates may go. Rates, in turn, influence mortgages, car loans, credit cards, and savings yields.
segments.tr: - **금리 기대치.** 연방준비제도는 PCE 물가지수라는 관련 지표로 측정한 2%의 인플레이션을 목표로 합니다. 시장은 여전히 더 일찍 발표되는 CPI를 금리가 어디로 향할지 알 수 있는 핵심 신호로 취급합니다. 금리는 다시 주택담보대출, 자동차 대출, 신용카드, 저축 수익률에 영향을 미칩니다.

segments.src: - **Social Security cost-of-living adjustments (COLAs).** The annual COLA is based on the CPI-W, a variant covering urban wage earners and clerical workers. It compares the third-quarter average with the prior year's third quarter.
segments.tr: - **사회보장 생활비 조정(COLA).** 연간 COLA는 도시 임금 근로자와 사무직 근로자를 다루는 변형인 CPI-W를 기반으로 합니다. 이는 3분기 평균을 전년도 3분기와 비교합니다.

segments.src: - **Wages and contracts.** Some labor agreements, leases, and benefit programs reference CPI changes, and inflation figures shape wage negotiations.
segments.tr: - **임금 및 계약.** 일부 노동 협약, 임대차 계약 및 혜택 프로그램은 CPI 변화를 참조하며, 인플레이션 수치는 임금 협상에 영향을 미칩니다.

segments.src: - **Tax and program parameters.** Federal income tax brackets and certain benefit thresholds are adjusted each year using a CPI-based measure.
segments.tr: - **세금 및 프로그램 매개변수.** 연방 소득세 과세 표준과 특정 혜택 임계값은 매년 CPI 기반 측정 지표를 사용하여 조정됩니다.

segments.src: ## Headline vs. Core: What's the Difference?
segments.tr: ## 헤드라인 대 코어: 차이점은 무엇인가요?

segments.src: **Headline CPI** covers everything in the basket.
segments.tr: **헤드라인 CPI**는 바구니에 담긴 모든 것을 다룹니다.

segments.src: **Core CPI** removes food and energy.
segments.tr: **코어 CPI**는 식품과 에너지를 제외합니다.

segments.src: Those two categories tend to swing sharply because of weather, crop conditions, geopolitical events, and oil-market shifts.
segments.tr: 이 두 범주는 날씨, 작황 조건, 지정학적 사건, 석유 시장 변화로 인해 급격히 흔들리는 경향이 있습니다.

segments.src: Stripping them out can give a steadier read on underlying trends, which is why many economists and policymakers watch core closely.
segments.tr: 이를 제외하면 기저 추세에 대한 더 안정적인 판독값을 제공할 수 있으며, 이것이 많은 경제학자와 정책 입안자들이 코어를 면밀히 주시하는 이유입니다.

segments.src: Core is not "the real inflation" and headline is not "the fake one."
segments.tr: 코어가 "진짜 인플레이션"은 아니며 헤드라인이 "가짜 인플레이션"은 아닙니다.

segments.src: They answer different questions:
segments.tr: 그들은 다른 질문에 답합니다:

segments.src: - Headline asks: *How much more does the typical household's total spending cost?*
segments.tr: - 헤드라인의 질문: *일반 가정의 총 지출 비용이 얼마나 더 증가했는가?*

segments.src: - Core asks: *Is price pressure broadening and persisting beyond volatile items?*
segments.tr: - 코어의 질문: *물가 압력이 변동성이 큰 품목을 넘어 광범위하고 지속적으로 나타나고 있는가?*

segments.src: Food and energy are not optional for most families, so a core reading that looks calm can sit alongside a headline reading that feels painful, and the reverse can also happen.
segments.tr: 식품과 에너지는 대부분의 가족에게 선택 사항이 아니므로, 차분해 보이는 코어 수치가 고통스럽게 느껴지는 헤드라인 수치와 나란히 존재할 수 있으며 그 반대의 경우도 발생할 수 있습니다.

segments.src: ## The Big Components, One by One
segments.tr: ## 주요 구성 요소 하나씩 살펴보기

segments.src: ### Shelter
segments.tr: ### 주거비

segments.src: Shelter is the largest piece of the index, typically around one-third of the overall CPI and a larger share of core.
segments.tr: 주거비는 지수의 가장 큰 비중을 차지하며, 일반적으로 전체 CPI의 약 3분의 1이고 코어에서 더 큰 비중을 차지합니다.

segments.src: It includes rent of primary residences and "owners' equivalent rent" (OER), which estimates what homeowners would pay to rent their own homes.
segments.tr: 여기에는 주거용 임대료와 주택 소유자가 자신의 집에 살 경우 지불해야 할 임대료를 추정하는 "소유자 등가 임대료(OER)"가 포함됩니다.

segments.src: It does not directly track home purchase prices or mortgage payments.
segments.tr: 주택 구입 가격이나 주택담보대출 상환금을 직접 추적하지는 않습니다.

segments.src: Two features matter when reading the report:
segments.tr: 보고서를 읽을 때 중요한 두 가지 특징은 다음과 같습니다:

segments.src: 1. **Lag.** Rent data are collected from a rotating sample, with each housing unit surveyed only periodically. As a result, the CPI can reflect changes in new-lease market rents months after private rent trackers show them.
segments.tr: 1. **시차.** 임대료 데이터는 순환 표본에서 수집되며, 각 주택 유닛은 주기적으로만 조사됩니다. 결과적으로 CPI는 민간 임대료 추적 기관이 신규 임대 시장 임대료의 변화를 보여준 후 수개월이 지난 후에야 이를 반영할 수 있습니다.

segments.src: 2. **Weight.** Because shelter is so big, a small monthly change can move core CPI noticeably.
segments.tr: 2. **가중치.** 주거비의 비중이 매우 크기 때문에 작은 월별 변화도 코어 CPI를 눈에 띄게 움직일 수 있습니다.

segments.src: If you rent, your experience may differ from the average, especially if your lease just renewed.
segments.tr: 세입자인 경우, 특히 임대차 계약이 막 갱신된 경우 경험이 평균과 다를 수 있습니다.

segments.src: If you own a home with a fixed-rate mortgage, your housing payment may barely change even while the index's shelter component rises.
segments.tr: 고정금리 주택담보대출을 받은 주택 소유자인 경우, 지수의 주거비 구성 요소가 상승하는 동안에도 주택 관련 지출은 거의 변하지 않을 수 있습니다.

segments.src: ### Food
segments.tr: ### 식품

segments.src: Food is split into "food at home" (groceries) and "food away from home" (restaurants and takeout).
segments.tr: 식품은 "가정 내 식품"(식료품)과 "외식"(식당 및 테이크아웃)으로 나뉩니다.

segments.src: Grocery prices can be volatile, driven by weather, animal disease, transportation costs, and global supply.
segments.tr: 식료품 가격은 날씨, 동물 질병, 운송 비용, 글로벌 공급망에 따라 변동성이 클 수 있습니다.

segments.src: Restaurant prices tend to move more steadily because they include labor and rent costs.
segments.tr: 식당 가격은 인건비와 임대료 비용을 포함하기 때문에 더 안정적으로 움직이는 경향이 있습니다.

segments.src: ### Energy
segments.tr: ### 에너지

segments.src: Energy covers gasoline, electricity, natural gas, and fuel oil.
segments.tr: 에너지는 휘발유, 전기, 천연가스, 난방유를 다룹니다.

segments.src: Gasoline often drives the largest month-to-month swings in headline inflation.
segments.tr: 휘발유는 헤드라인 인플레이션에서 월별 변동 폭이 가장 큰 경우가 많습니다.

segments.src: A drop at the pump can pull the headline number down even if nothing else has changed, and a spike can do the opposite.
segments.tr: 주유소 가격의 하락은 다른 것이 전혀 변하지 않았더라도 헤드라인 수치를 끌어내릴 수 있으며, 급등은 그 반대의 역할을 할 수 있습니다.

segments.src: ### Core goods and core services
segments.tr: ### 코어 상품 및 코어 서비스

segments.src: Within core, economists often separate **goods** (cars, furniture, apparel, appliances) from **services** (medical care, insurance, transportation services, recreation, and shelter).
segments.tr: 코어 내에서 경제학자들은 종종 **상품**(자동차, 가구, 의류, 가전제품)과 **서비스**(의료, 보험, 운송 서비스, 오락, 주거비)를 구분합니다.

segments.src: Goods prices respond strongly to supply chains and tariffs, while services tend to be tied to wages and move more slowly.
segments.tr: 상품 가격은 공급망과 관세에 강하게 반응하는 반면, 서비스는 임금과 연동되어 더 천천히 움직이는 경향이 있습니다.

segments.src: A report in which "supercore" services (core services excluding housing) stays elevated may signal different pressures than one driven by goods.
segments.tr: "슈퍼코어" 서비스(주택을 제외한 코어 서비스)가 높은 수준을 유지하는 보고서는 상품에 의해 주도되는 보고서와는 다른 압력을 시사할 수 있습니다.

segments.src: ## How to Read the Report in Five Steps
segments.tr: ## 보고서를 읽는 5단계 방법

segments.src: 1. **Check the monthly change first.** The monthly figure, seasonally adjusted, shows the latest momentum. The annual (year-over-year) figure covers twelve months and can be influenced by what happened a year ago, a quirk known as the *base effect*.
segments.tr: 1. **월간 변화를 먼저 확인하세요.** 계절 조정된 월간 수치는 가장 최근의 모멘텀을 보여줍니다. 연간(전년 동기 대비) 수치는 12개월을 다루며 1년 전에 일어난 일의 영향을 받을 수 있는데, 이를 *기저 효과*라고 합니다.

segments.src: 2. **Compare headline and core.** A wide gap usually points to food or energy as the cause.
segments.tr: 2. **헤드라인과 코어를 비교하세요.** 격차가 크다면 대개 식품이나 에너지가 원인임을 나타냅니다.

segments.src: 3. **Look at shelter.** Is it rising or easing, and how much of the core change does it explain?
segments.tr: 3. **주거비를 살펴보세요.** 상승하고 있는지 완화되고 있는지, 그리고 코어 변화의 얼마나 많은 부분을 설명하고 있는지 확인하세요.

segments.src: 4. **Look beyond the headline.** Goods, services excluding shelter, and categories you personally buy tell you more than a single number.
segments.tr: 4. **헤드라인 너머를 보세요.** 상품, 주거비를 제외한 서비스, 그리고 개인이 직접 구매하는 카테고리는 단일 숫자보다 더 많은 것을 말해줍니다.

segments.src: 5. **Compare with expectations.** Markets react to the gap between the reported figure and forecasts, not just the figure itself. A "hot" or "cool" label usually means above or below the consensus estimate, and the numbers are often revised or rounded in ways that make small misses look bigger than they are.
segments.tr: 5. **예상치와 비교하세요.** 시장은 숫자 자체뿐만 아니라 보고된 수치와 예측 사이의 격차에 반응합니다. "핫" 또는 "쿨"이라는 라벨은 대개 컨센서스 추정치보다 높거나 낮음을 의미하며, 숫자는 종종 작은 실수가 더 커 보이게 만드는 방식으로 수정되거나 반올림됩니다.

segments.src: For a smoother view, some analysts follow alternative measures such as the Cleveland Fed's median and trimmed-mean CPI, which reduce the influence of extreme price moves.
segments.tr: 더 부드러운 보기를 위해 일부 분석가는 극단적인 가격 변동의 영향을 줄이는 클리블랜드 연은의 중앙값 및 절사 평균 CPI와 같은 대체 측정항목을 따릅니다.

segments.src: ## Why the Official Number Can Miss What You Pay
segments.tr: ## 공식 수치가 내가 지불하는 비용을 놓칠 수 있는 이유

segments.src: Even a well-built index describes an average that no real household matches exactly.
segments.tr: 잘 만들어진 지수조차도 실제 가계가 정확히 일치하지 않는 평균을 설명합니다.

segments.src: Several reasons explain the mismatch:
segments.tr: 이러한 불일치를 설명하는 몇 가지 이유는 다음과 같습니다:

segments.src: - **Your basket is different.** The CPI weights categories by typical spending. If you commute long distances, have young children, pay for private insurance, or rent in a fast-moving market, your mix may lean toward faster-rising items.
segments.tr: - **당신의 바구니는 다릅니다.** CPI는 일반적인 지출에 따라 카테고리의 가중치를 부여합니다. 장거리 출퇴근을 하거나, 어린 자녀가 있거나, 사보험 비용을 지불하거나, 빠르게 움직이는 시장에서 임대하는 경우, 당신의 소비 조합은 빠르게 상승하는 품목으로 기울 수 있습니다.

segments.src: - **Prices vs. inflation.** Inflation is a rate of change. When inflation slows from, say, a high rate to a lower one, prices are still rising, just more slowly. Price *levels* generally do not fall back, so everyday costs can still feel high long after the annual rate has eased.
segments.tr: - **가격 대 인플레이션.** 인플레이션은 변화율입니다. 인플레이션이 높은 수준에서 낮은 수준으로 둔화될 때에도 가격은 여전히 상승하고 있으며, 다만 더 천천히 오를 뿐입니다. 가격 *수준*은 일반적으로 다시 떨어지지 않기 때문에 연간 상승률이 둔화된 지 오래되었어도 일상 비용은 여전히 높게 느껴질 수 있습니다.

segments.src: - **Frequent purchases loom larger.** People notice gas, eggs, and coffee more than they notice the price of a washing machine bought once every ten years. Frequent, visible purchases shape perception more than their budget share would suggest.
segments.tr: - **자주 구매하는 품목이 더 크게 다가옵니다.** 사람들은 10년에 한 번 사는 세탁기 가격보다 휘발유, 달걀, 커피를 더 많이 체감합니다. 빈번하고 눈에 띄는 구매는 예산 비중이 시사하는 것보다 인체 인큐베이터 인식을 더 많이 형성합니다.

segments.src: - **Quality adjustments.** The BLS adjusts prices when product quality changes, such as a phone with a better camera. This is intended to separate pure price changes from improvements, but consumers may not feel they are getting the extra value.
segments.tr: - **품질 조정.** BLS는 더 나은 카메라가 장착된 휴대폰과 같이 제품 품질이 변경될 때 가격을 조정합니다. 이는 순수 가격 변화와 개선 사항을 분리하기 위한 것이지만, 소비자는 추가 가치를 얻고 있다고 느끼지 못할 수 있습니다.

segments.src: - **Shrinkflation and substitution.** Smaller packages at the same price are captured in the unit-price data, but the index also assumes consumers shift to alternatives when relative prices change. Not everyone can or wants to switch.
segments.tr: - **슈링크플레이션과 대체.** 동일한 가격의 더 작은 패키지는 단위 가격 데이터에 포착되지만, 이 지수는 상대 가격이 변할 때 소비자가 대체재로 전환한다고 가정합니다. 모든 사람이 전환할 수 있거나 전환하기를 원하는 것은 아닙니다.

segments.src: - **Regional differences.** National averages mask local conditions. Housing, utilities, and insurance costs vary widely by metro area.
segments.tr: - **지역적 차이.** 국가 평균은 지역적 상황을 가립니다. 주택, 공공요금, 보험 비용은 대도시 지역에 따라 크게 다릅니다.

segments.src: - **Income and wage timing.** If your pay rises slower than prices, you feel the squeeze regardless of what the index says; if it rises faster, the squeeze may feel milder.
segments.tr: - **소득 및 임금 시기.** 급여가 물가보다 느리게 오르면 지수가 무엇을 말하든 압박감을 느끼게 되며, 더 빨리 오르면 압박감이 덜하게 느껴질 수 있습니다.

segments.src: ## A Practical Way to Build Your Own Inflation Read
segments.tr: ## 나만의 인플레이션 읽기를 구축하는 실용적인 방법

segments.src: - List your top spending categories and what you paid for each over the past year.
segments.tr: - 주요 지출 카테고리와 작년에 각각 얼마를 지불했는지 나열하세요.

segments.src: - Compare those with the matching CPI components, which the BLS publishes in detail, including regional tables.
segments.tr: - 지역별 표를 포함하여 BLS가 자세히 게시하는 일치하는 CPI 구성 요소와 이를 비교하세요.

segments.src: - Note which costs are fixed (a fixed-rate mortgage, a locked lease) and which are exposed (groceries, fuel, insurance renewals).
segments.tr: - 어떤 비용이 고정되어 있고(고정금리 주택담보대출, 고정 임대차 계약) 어떤 비용이 노출되어 있는지(식료품, 연료, 보험 갱신) 주목하세요.

segments.src: - Use the result for budgeting and for conversations about pay, rather than relying on a single national percentage.
segments.tr: - 단일 국가 백분율에 의존하기보다는 예산 편성 및 급여 관련 대화에 결과를 사용하세요.

segments.src: ## The Bottom Line
segments.tr: ## 결론

segments.src: The CPI is a valuable, carefully constructed tool, but it is an average of a basket, not a bill of your own.
segments.tr: CPI는 가치 있고 신중하게 구축된 도구이지만, 바구니의 평균이지 자신의 청구서가 아닙니다.

segments.src: Headline inflation tells you how much the full basket moved; core inflation helps you see how persistent the underlying pressure is; and shelter, food, and energy each tell a different part of the story.
segments.tr: 헤드라인 인플레이션은 전체 바구니가 얼마나 움직였는지 알려주고, 코어 인플레이션은 기저 압력이 얼마나 지속되는지 보는 데 도움이 되며, 주거비, 식품, 에너지는 각각 이야기의 다른 부분을 말해줍니다.

segments.src: Reading the next report with those distinctions in mind will help you separate noise from trend, and explain why the data and your wallet sometimes seem to disagree.
segments.tr: 이러한 구분을 염두에 두고 다음 보고서를 읽으면 노이즈와 트렌드를 구분하고 데이터와 지갑이 왜 때때로 일치하지 않아 보이는지 설명하는 데 도움이 될 것입니다.

zh.title: 总体CPI与核心CPI：如何解读下一次CPI报告以及为什么你的生活成本感觉不同

segments.src: Once a month, usually at 8:30 a.m.
segments.tr: 每月一次，通常在月中某个工作日的上午 8:30

segments.src: Eastern on a weekday around the middle of the month, the U.S.
segments.tr: 美东时间，美国

segments.src: Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) publishes the Consumer Price Index (CPI).
segments.tr: 劳工统计局 (BLS) 会发布消费者价格指数 (CPI)。

segments.src: Within minutes, headlines announce whether inflation "cooled," "reheated," or "surprised."
segments.tr: 几分钟之内，各大头条新闻就会宣布通货膨胀是“降温”、“回升”还是“意外”。

segments.src: Yet many readers look at their own grocery receipts, rent, and gas bills and wonder why the official number doesn't match their experience.
segments.tr: 然而，许多读者看着自己的杂货收据、房租和天然气账单，不禁疑惑为什么官方数字与他们的实际感受不符。

segments.src: This guide explains what the CPI measures, how the headline and core readings differ, what each major category contributes, and why your personal inflation rate can differ from the national figure.
segments.tr: 本指南解释了 CPI 衡量的内容、总体读数与核心读数的区别、每个主要类别的影响，以及为什么你的个人通胀率会与国家数据有所不同。

segments.src: It is educational background, not financial advice.
segments.tr: 这是教育背景知识，而非财务建议。

segments.src: ## Why the CPI Matters
segments.tr: ## 为什么 CPI 很重要

segments.src: The CPI tracks the average change over time in prices paid by urban consumers for a fixed basket of goods and services.
segments.tr: CPI 追踪城市消费者为购买一篮子固定的商品和服务所支付的价格随时间推移的平均变化。

segments.src: It feeds into several things that touch daily life:
segments.tr: 它影响着日常生活的几个方面：

segments.src: - **Interest-rate expectations.** The Federal Reserve targets 2% inflation, measured by a related gauge called the PCE price index. Markets still treat the CPI, which arrives earlier, as a key signal for where rates may go. Rates, in turn, influence mortgages, car loans, credit cards, and savings yields.
segments.tr: - **利率预期。** 美联储的目标是将通胀率控制在 2%，这由相关的 PCE 价格指数来衡量。市场仍然将较早发布的 CPI 视为利率走向的关键信号。而利率反过来又会影响抵押贷款、汽车贷款、信用卡和储蓄收益率。

segments.src: - **Social Security cost-of-living adjustments (COLAs).** The annual COLA is based on the CPI-W, a variant covering urban wage earners and clerical workers. It compares the third-quarter average with the prior year's third quarter.
segments.tr: - **社会保障生活成本调整 (COLA)。** 年度 COLA 基于 CPI-W，这是涵盖城市工薪阶层和文职人员的变体。它将第三季度平均值与前一年第三季度进行比较。

segments.src: - **Wages and contracts.** Some labor agreements, leases, and benefit programs reference CPI changes, and inflation figures shape wage negotiations.
segments.tr: - **工资和合同。** 一些劳工协议、租约和福利项目参考了 CPI 的变化，通胀数据也会影响工资谈判。

segments.src: - **Tax and program parameters.** Federal income tax brackets and certain benefit thresholds are adjusted each year using a CPI-based measure.
segments.tr: - **税收和项目参数。** 联邦所得税税率阶梯和某些福利门槛每年都会使用基于 CPI 的指标进行调整。

segments.src: ## Headline vs. Core: What's the Difference?
segments.tr: ## 总体 CPI 与核心 CPI：有什么区别？

segments.src: **Headline CPI** covers everything in the basket.
segments.tr: **总体 CPI** 涵盖篮子中的所有内容。

segments.src: **Core CPI** removes food and energy.
segments.tr: **核心 CPI** 剔除了食品和能源。

segments.src: Those two categories tend to swing sharply because of weather, crop conditions, geopolitical events, and oil-market shifts.
segments.tr: 由于天气、农作物状况、地缘政治事件和石油市场变化，这两个类别往往会剧烈波动。

segments.src: Stripping them out can give a steadier read on underlying trends, which is why many economists and policymakers watch core closely.
segments.tr: 剔除它们可以更稳定地了解潜在趋势，这就是许多经济学家和政策制定者密切关注核心通胀的原因。

segments.src: Core is not "the real inflation" and headline is not "the fake one."
segments.tr: 核心通胀并非“真正的通胀”，总体通胀也不是“虚假的通胀”。

segments.src: They answer different questions:
segments.tr: 它们回答不同的问题：

segments.src: - Headline asks: *How much more does the typical household's total spending cost?*
segments.tr: - 总体 CPI 询问：*典型家庭的总支出成本增加了多少？*

segments.src: - Core asks: *Is price pressure broadening and persisting beyond volatile items?*
segments.tr: - 核心 CPI 询问：*价格压力是否在扩大并在波动性项目之外持续存在？*

segments.src: Food and energy are not optional for most families, so a core reading that looks calm can sit alongside a headline reading that feels painful, and the reverse can also happen.
segments.tr: 对大多数家庭来说，食品和能源并非可选项，因此看起来平稳的核心读数可能与让人感到痛苦的总体读数并存，反之亦然。

segments.src: ## The Big Components, One by One
segments.tr: ## 各大组成部分逐一解析

segments.src: ### Shelter
segments.tr: ### 住房

segments.src: Shelter is the largest piece of the index, typically around one-third of the overall CPI and a larger share of core.
segments.tr: 住房是指数中最大的一部分，通常占整个 CPI 的三分之一左右，在核心 CPI 中占比更大。

segments.src: It includes rent of primary residences and "owners' equivalent rent" (OER), which estimates what homeowners would pay to rent their own homes.
segments.tr: 它包括主要住宅的租金和“业主等价租金”(OER)，后者估计了业主为租用自己的房屋需要支付的费用。

segments.src: It does not directly track home purchase prices or mortgage payments.
segments.tr: 它不直接追踪购房价格或抵押贷款支付。

segments.src: Two features matter when reading the report:
segments.tr: 在解读报告时，有两个特征很重要：

segments.src: 1. **Lag.** Rent data are collected from a rotating sample, with each housing unit surveyed only periodically. As a result, the CPI can reflect changes in new-lease market rents months after private rent trackers show them.
segments.tr: 1. **滞后性。** 租金数据是从轮换样本中收集的，每个住房单元仅定期进行调查。因此，CPI 反映新租约市场租金变化的时间可能会比私人租金追踪机构显示的时间晚几个月。

segments.src: 2. **Weight.** Because shelter is so big, a small monthly change can move core CPI noticeably.
segments.tr: 2. **权重。** 由于住房占比非常大，微小的月度变化就能明显推动核心 CPI。

segments.src: If you rent, your experience may differ from the average, especially if your lease just renewed.
segments.tr: 如果你是租房者，你的体验可能与平均水平不同，特别是如果你的租约刚刚续签的话。

segments.src: If you own a home with a fixed-rate mortgage, your housing payment may barely change even while the index's shelter component rises.
segments.tr: 如果你拥有带有固定利率抵押贷款的房屋，即使指数的住房部分上升，你的住房支出也可能几乎没有变化。

segments.src: ### Food
segments.tr: ### 食品

segments.src: Food is split into "food at home" (groceries) and "food away from home" (restaurants and takeout).
segments.tr: 食品分为“居家食品”（杂货）和“外出就餐”（餐馆和外卖）。

segments.src: Grocery prices can be volatile, driven by weather, animal disease, transportation costs, and global supply.
segments.tr: 受天气、动物疾病、运输成本和全球供应链的驱动，杂货价格可能会波动。

segments.src: Restaurant prices tend to move more steadily because they include labor and rent costs.
segments.tr: 餐馆价格往往变动更稳定，因为它们包含人工和租金成本。

segments.src: ### Energy
segments.tr: ### 能源

segments.src: Energy covers gasoline, electricity, natural gas, and fuel oil.
segments.tr: 能源涵盖汽油、电力、天然气和燃料油。

segments.src: Gasoline often drives the largest month-to-month swings in headline inflation.
segments.tr: 汽油通常推动总体通胀最大的月度波动。

segments.src: A drop at the pump can pull the headline number down even if nothing else has changed, and a spike can do the opposite.
segments.tr: 即使其他一切都没有改变，加油站价格的下跌也会将总体数字拉低，而飙升则会产生相反的效果。

segments.src: ### Core goods and core services
segments.tr: ### 核心商品与核心服务

segments.src: Within core, economists often separate **goods** (cars, furniture, apparel, appliances) from **services** (medical care, insurance, transportation services, recreation, and shelter).
segments.tr: 在核心通胀中，经济学家通常将**商品**（汽车、家具、服装、家电）与**服务**（医疗保健、保险、运输服务、娱乐和住房）分开。

segments.src: Goods prices respond strongly to supply chains and tariffs, while services tend to be tied to wages and move more slowly.
segments.tr: 商品价格对供应链和关税反应强烈，而服务价格往往与工资挂钩且变动较慢。

segments.src: A report in which "supercore" services (core services excluding housing) stays elevated may signal different pressures than one driven by goods.
segments.tr: “超级核心”服务（不包括住房的核心服务）保持高位的报告可能预示着与商品驱动的报告不同的压力。

segments.src: ## How to Read the Report in Five Steps
segments.tr: ## 分五步解读报告

segments.src: 1. **Check the monthly change first.** The monthly figure, seasonally adjusted, shows the latest momentum. The annual (year-over-year) figure covers twelve months and can be influenced by what happened a year ago, a quirk known as the *base effect*.
segments.tr: 1. **首先检查月度变化。** 经过季节性调整的月度数据反映了最新的动能。年度（同比）数据涵盖十二个月，可能会受到一年前发生的事情的影响，这种怪现象被称为*基数效应*。

segments.src: 2. **Compare headline and core.** A wide gap usually points to food or energy as the cause.
segments.tr: 2. **比较总体和核心。** 巨大的差距通常指向食品或能源是罪魁祸首。

segments.src: 3. **Look at shelter.** Is it rising or easing, and how much of the core change does it explain?
segments.tr: 3. **看住房。** 它是在上升还是在缓解，它解释了多少核心变动？

segments.src: 4. **Look beyond the headline.** Goods, services excluding shelter, and categories you personally buy tell you more than a single number.
segments.tr: 4. **超越总体数据。** 商品、不含住房的服务以及你个人购买的类别比单一数字更能告诉你真实情况。

segments.src: 5. **Compare with expectations.** Markets react to the gap between the reported figure and forecasts, not just the figure itself. A "hot" or "cool" label usually means above or below the consensus estimate, and the numbers are often revised or rounded in ways that make small misses look bigger than they are.
segments.tr: 5. **与预期进行比较。** 市场对报告数字与预测之间的差距做出反应，而不仅仅是数字本身。“高”或“低”的标签通常意味着高于或低于共识估计，而且这些数字经常以某种方式进行修正或四舍五入，使得微小的偏差看起来比实际更大。

segments.src: For a smoother view, some analysts follow alternative measures such as the Cleveland Fed's median and trimmed-mean CPI, which reduce the influence of extreme price moves.
segments.tr: 为了获得更平稳的视图，一些分析师会关注替代指标，例如克利夫兰联储的中位数和截尾均值 CPI，这减少了极端价格变动的影响。

segments.src: ## Why the Official Number Can Miss What You Pay
segments.tr: ## 为什么官方数字会忽略你的实际支出

segments.src: Even a well-built index describes an average that no real household matches exactly.
segments.tr: 即使是构建良好的指数也只能描述没有哪个真实家庭完全匹配的平均值。

segments.src: Several reasons explain the mismatch:
segments.tr: 有几个原因可以解释这种不匹配：

segments.src: - **Your basket is different.** The CPI weights categories by typical spending. If you commute long distances, have young children, pay for private insurance, or rent in a fast-moving market, your mix may lean toward faster-rising items.
segments.tr: - **你的消费篮子不同。** CPI 根据典型支出来给各个类别加权。如果你通勤距离长、有幼儿、支付私人保险费用或在瞬息万变的市场中租房，你的消费组合可能倾向于价格上涨更快的项目。

segments.src: - **Prices vs. inflation.** Inflation is a rate of change. When inflation slows from, say, a high rate to a lower one, prices are still rising, just more slowly. Price *levels* generally do not fall back, so everyday costs can still feel high long after the annual rate has eased.
segments.tr: - **价格与通胀。** 通胀是变化率。当通胀从高位放缓至较低水平时，价格仍在上涨，只是速度变慢了。价格*水平*通常不会回落，因此在年度通胀率放缓很久之后，日常成本可能仍然感觉很高。

segments.src: - **Frequent purchases loom larger.** People notice gas, eggs, and coffee more than they notice the price of a washing machine bought once every ten years. Frequent, visible purchases shape perception more than their budget share would suggest.
segments.tr: - **频繁购买的物品影响更大。** 人们对汽油、鸡蛋和咖啡的关注度高于十年买一次的洗衣机价格。频繁、可见的购买比其预算份额所暗示的更能塑造感知。

segments.src: - **Quality adjustments.** The BLS adjusts prices when product quality changes, such as a phone with a better camera. This is intended to separate pure price changes from improvements, but consumers may not feel they are getting the extra value.
segments.tr: - **质量调整。** 当产品质量发生变化时，BLS 会调整价格，例如配备更好摄像头的手机。这旨在将纯粹的价格变动与改进分开，但消费者可能并不觉得他们获得了额外的价值。

segments.src: - **Shrinkflation and substitution.** Smaller packages at the same price are captured in the unit-price data, but the index also assumes consumers shift to alternatives when relative prices change. Not everyone can or wants to switch.
segments.tr: - **隐性通胀与替代。** 价格相同但包装变小的数据会被单位价格数据捕捉到，但该指数还假设当相对价格发生变化时，消费者会转向替代品。并非每个人都能或愿意转换。

segments.src: - **Regional differences.** National averages mask local conditions. Housing, utilities, and insurance costs vary widely by metro area.
segments.tr: - **地区差异。** 国家平均水平掩盖了地方情况。住房、公用事业和保险费用因大都市区而异。

segments.src: - **Income and wage timing.** If your pay rises slower than prices, you feel the squeeze regardless of what the index says; if it rises faster, the squeeze may feel milder.
segments.tr: - **收入和工资发放时间。** 如果你的工资涨幅低于物价涨幅，无论指数怎么说，你都会感到压力；如果涨幅更快，压力可能会感觉更温和。

segments.src: ## A Practical Way to Build Your Own Inflation Read
segments.tr: ## 构建你自己的通胀解读的实用方法

segments.src: - List your top spending categories and what you paid for each over the past year.
segments.tr: - 列出你的主要支出类别以及过去一年中为每项支付的费用。

segments.src: - Compare those with the matching CPI components, which the BLS publishes in detail, including regional tables.
segments.tr: - 将这些与匹配的 CPI 组件进行比较，BLS 对这些组件进行了详细发布，包括区域表格。

segments.src: - Note which costs are fixed (a fixed-rate mortgage, a locked lease) and which are exposed (groceries, fuel, insurance renewals).
segments.tr: - 注意哪些成本是固定的（固定利率抵押贷款、锁定的租约），哪些是敞口的（杂货、燃料、保险续签）。

segments.src: - Use the result for budgeting and for conversations about pay, rather than relying on a single national percentage.
segments.tr: - 将结果用于预算编制和工资讨论，而不是依赖单一的国家百分比。

segments.src: ## The Bottom Line
segments.tr: ## 底线

segments.src: The CPI is a valuable, carefully constructed tool, but it is an average of a basket, not a bill of your own.
segments.tr: CPI 是一个宝贵且经过精心构建的工具，但它是一篮子商品的平均值，而不是你自己的账单。

segments.src: Headline inflation tells you how much the full basket moved; core inflation helps you see how persistent the underlying pressure is; and shelter, food, and energy each tell a different part of the story.
segments.tr: 总体通胀告诉你整个篮子的变动幅度；核心通胀帮助你了解潜在压力的持续性；住房、食品和能源各自讲述了故事的不同部分。

segments.src: Reading the next report with those distinctions in mind will help you separate noise from trend, and explain why the data and your wallet sometimes seem to disagree.
segments.tr: 带着这些区别阅读下一份报告将帮助你区分噪音与趋势，并解释为什么数据和你的钱包有时似乎存在分歧。

segments.src: Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) publishes the Consumer Price Index (CPI).
segments.tr: ब्यूरो ऑफ लेबर स्टैटिस्टिक्स (बीएलएस) उपभोक्ता मूल्य सूचकांक (सीपीआई) प्रकाशित करता है।

segments.src: Within minutes, headlines announce whether inflation "cooled," "reheated," or "surprised."
segments.tr: कुछ ही मिनटों में, सुर्खियां यह घोषणा करती हैं कि मुद्रास्फीति "ठंडी हुई", "फिर से गर्म हुई", या "आश्चर्यचकित किया"।

segments.src: Yet many readers look at their own grocery receipts, rent, and gas bills and wonder why the official number doesn't match their experience.
segments.tr: फिर भी कई पाठक अपनी किराने की रसीदें, किराए और गैस बिलों को देखते हैं और सोचते हैं कि आधिकारिक संख्या उनके अनुभव से मेल क्यों नहीं खाती है।

segments.src: This guide explains what the CPI measures, how the headline and core readings differ, what each major category contributes, and why your personal inflation rate can differ from the national figure.
segments.tr: यह मार्गदर्शिका बताती है कि सीपीआई क्या मापता है, हेडलाइन और कोर रीडिंग कैसे भिन्न होती हैं, प्रत्येक प्रमुख श्रेणी क्या योगदान देती है, और आपकी व्यक्तिगत मुद्रास्फीति दर राष्ट्रीय आंकड़े से क्यों भिन्न हो सकती है।

segments.src: It is educational background, not financial advice.
segments.tr: यह शैक्षिक पृष्ठभूमि है, वित्तीय सलाह नहीं।

segments.src: ## Why the CPI Matters
segments.tr: ## सीपीआई क्यों महत्वपूर्ण है

segments.src: The CPI tracks the average change over time in prices paid by urban consumers for a fixed basket of goods and services.
segments.tr: सीपीआई वस्तुओं और सेवाओं की एक निश्चित टोकरी के लिए शहरी उपभोक्ताओं द्वारा भुगतान की जाने वाली कीमतों में समय के साथ औसत परिवर्तन को ट्रैक करता है।

segments.src: It feeds into several things that touch daily life:
segments.tr: यह दैनिक जीवन को छूने वाली कई चीजों में योगदान देता है:

segments.src: - **Interest-rate expectations.** The Federal Reserve targets 2% inflation, measured by a related gauge called the PCE price index. Markets still treat the CPI, which arrives earlier, as a key signal for where rates may go. Rates, in turn, influence mortgages, car loans, credit cards, and savings yields.
segments.tr: - **ब्याज दर की उम्मीदें।** फेडरल रिजर्व 2% मुद्रास्फीति का लक्ष्य रखता है, जिसे पीसीई मूल्य सूचकांक नामक एक संबंधित गेज द्वारा मापा जाता है। बाजार अभी भी सीपीआई को, जो पहले आता है, दरों के जाने की दिशा के लिए एक प्रमुख संकेत के रूप में मानते हैं। बदले में दरें, बंधक, कार ऋण, क्रेडिट कार्ड और बचत यील्ड को प्रभावित करती हैं।

segments.src: - **Social Security cost-of-living adjustments (COLAs).** The annual COLA is based on the CPI-W, a variant covering urban wage earners and clerical workers. It compares the third-quarter average with the prior year's third quarter.
segments.tr: - **सामाजिक सुरक्षा जीवन-यापन लागत समायोजन (COLAs)।** वार्षिक कोला (COLA) सीपीआई-डब्ल्यू पर आधारित है, जो शहरी वेतन भोगियों और लिपिकीय श्रमिकों को कवर करने वाला एक प्रकार है। यह पिछली तीसरी तिमाही के साथ तीसरी तिमाही के औसत की तुलना करता है।

segments.src: - **Wages and contracts.** Some labor agreements, leases, and benefit programs reference CPI changes, and inflation figures shape wage negotiations.
segments.tr: - **वेतन और अनुबंध।** कुछ श्रम समझौते, पट्टे और लाभ कार्यक्रम सीपीआई परिवर्तनों का संदर्भ देते हैं, और मुद्रास्फीति के आंकड़े वेतन वार्ताओं को आकार देते हैं।

segments.src: - **Tax and program parameters.** Federal income tax brackets and certain benefit thresholds are adjusted each year using a CPI-based measure.
segments.tr: - **कर और कार्यक्रम पैरामीटर।** संघीय आयकर ब्रैकेट और कुछ लाभ की सीमाएं हर साल सीपीआई-आधारित माप का उपयोग करके समायोजित की जाती हैं।

segments.src: ## Headline vs. Core: What's the Difference?
segments.tr: ## हेडलाइन बनाम कोर: अंतर क्या है?

segments.src: **Headline CPI** covers everything in the basket.
segments.tr: **हेडलाइन सीपीआई** टोकरी में सब कुछ कवर करता है।

segments.src: **Core CPI** removes food and energy.
segments.tr: **कोर सीपीआई** भोजन और ऊर्जा को हटा देता है।

segments.src: Those two categories tend to swing sharply because of weather, crop conditions, geopolitical events, and oil-market shifts.
segments.tr: मौसम, फसल की स्थिति, भू-राजनीतिक घटनाओं और तेल बाजार के बदलावों के कारण वे दो श्रेणियां तेजी से बदलती हैं।

segments.src: Stripping them out can give a steadier read on underlying trends, which is why many economists and policymakers watch core closely.
segments.tr: उन्हें हटाने से अंतर्निहित प्रवृत्तियों पर एक स्थिर पठन मिल सकता है, यही कारण है कि कई अर्थशास्त्री और नीति निर्माता कोर पर करीब से नजर रखते हैं।

segments.src: Core is not "the real inflation" and headline is not "the fake one."
segments.tr: कोर "वास्तविक मुद्रास्फीति" नहीं है और हेडलाइन "नकली" नहीं है।

segments.src: They answer different questions:
segments.tr: वे अलग-अलग सवालों के जवाब देते हैं:

segments.src: - Headline asks: *How much more does the typical household's total spending cost?*
segments.tr: - हेडलाइन पूछता है: *विशिष्ट परिवार के कुल खर्च की लागत कितनी अधिक है?*

segments.src: - Core asks: *Is price pressure broadening and persisting beyond volatile items?*
segments.tr: - कोर पूछता है: *क्या मूल्य दबाव अस्थिर वस्तुओं से परे व्यापक और निरंतर हो रहा है?*

segments.src: Food and energy are not optional for most families, so a core reading that looks calm can sit alongside a headline reading that feels painful, and the reverse can also happen.
segments.tr: अधिकांश परिवारों के लिए भोजन और ऊर्जा वैकल्पिक नहीं हैं, इसलिए एक कोर रीडिंग जो शांत दिखती है, एक हेडलाइन रीडिंग के साथ बैठ सकती है जो दर्दनाक महसूस होती है, और इसके विपरीत भी हो सकता है।

segments.src: ## The Big Components, One by One
segments.tr: ## बड़े घटक, एक-एक करके

segments.src: ### Shelter
segments.tr: ### आवास

segments.src: Shelter is the largest piece of the index, typically around one-third of the overall CPI and a larger share of core.
segments.tr: आवास सूचकांक का सबसे बड़ा हिस्सा है, जो आमतौर पर समग्र सीपीआई का लगभग एक तिहाई और कोर का एक बड़ा हिस्सा है।

segments.src: It includes rent of primary residences and "owners' equivalent rent" (OER), which estimates what homeowners would pay to rent their own homes.
segments.tr: इसमें प्राथमिक आवासों का किराया और "मालिकों का समतुल्य किराया" (OER) शामिल है, जो यह अनुमान लगाता है कि मकान मालिक अपने घरों को किराए पर देने के लिए कितना भुगतान करेंगे।

segments.src: It does not directly track home purchase prices or mortgage payments.
segments.tr: यह सीधे घर की खरीद की कीमतों या बंधक भुगतान को ट्रैक नहीं करता है।

segments.src: Two features matter when reading the report:
segments.tr: रिपोर्ट पढ़ते समय दो विशेषताएं मायने रखती हैं:

segments.src: 1. **Lag.** Rent data are collected from a rotating sample, with each housing unit surveyed only periodically. As a result, the CPI can reflect changes in new-lease market rents months after private rent trackers show them.
segments.tr: 1. **लैग।** किराए का डेटा एक घूर्णन नमूने से एकत्र किया जाता है, प्रत्येक आवास इकाई का सर्वेक्षण केवल समय-समय पर किया जाता है। परिणामस्वरूप, सीपीआई निजी किराए के ट्रैकर्स द्वारा दिखाने के महीनों बाद नए-लीज बाजार किराए में बदलाव को प्रतिबिंबित कर सकता है।

segments.src: 2. **Weight.** Because shelter is so big, a small monthly change can move core CPI noticeably.
segments.tr: 2. **भार।** चूंकि आवास बहुत बड़ा है, एक छोटा मासिक परिवर्तन कोर सीपीआई को उल्लेखनीय रूप से स्थानांतरित कर सकता है।

segments.src: If you rent, your experience may differ from the average, especially if your lease just renewed.
segments.tr: यदि आप किराए पर लेते हैं, तो आपका अनुभव औसत से भिन्न हो सकता है, खासकर यदि आपका पट्टा अभी नवीनीकृत हुआ है।

segments.src: If you own a home with a fixed-rate mortgage, your housing payment may barely change even while the index's shelter component rises.
segments.tr: यदि आप निश्चित-दर बंधक के साथ घर के मालिक हैं, तो आपका आवास भुगतान मुश्किल से बदल सकता है, भले ही सूचकांक का आवास घटक बढ़ जाए।

segments.src: ### Food
segments.tr: ### भोजन

segments.src: Food is split into "food at home" (groceries) and "food away from home" (restaurants and takeout).
segments.tr: भोजन को "घर पर भोजन" (किराना) और "घर से दूर भोजन" (रेस्तरां और टेकअवे) में विभाजित किया गया है।

segments.src: Grocery prices can be volatile, driven by weather, animal disease, transportation costs, and global supply.
segments.tr: मौसम, पशु रोग, परिवहन लागत और वैश्विक आपूर्ति से प्रेरित होकर किराने की कीमतें अस्थिर हो सकती हैं।

segments.src: Restaurant prices tend to move more steadily because they include labor and rent costs.
segments.tr: रेस्तरां की कीमतें अधिक लगातार बढ़ने लगती हैं क्योंकि उनमें श्रम और किराए की लागत शामिल होती है।

segments.src: ### Energy
Energy covers gasoline, electricity, natural gas, and fuel oil.
segments.tr: ऊर्जा में गैसोलीन, बिजली, प्राकृतिक गैस और ईंधन तेल शामिल हैं।

segments.src: Gasoline often drives the largest month-to-month swings in headline inflation.
segments.tr: गैसोलीन अक्सर हेडलाइन मुद्रास्फीति में सबसे बड़ा महीने-दर-महीने उतार-चढ़ाव चलाता है।

segments.src: A drop at the pump can pull the headline number down even if nothing else has changed, and a spike can do the opposite.
segments.tr: पंप पर गिरावट हेडलाइन नंबर को नीचे खींच सकती है, भले ही कुछ भी नहीं बदला हो, और एक स्पाइक इसके विपरीत कर सकता है।

segments.src: ### Core goods and core services
segments.tr: ### कोर सामान और कोर सेवाएं

segments.src: Within core, economists often separate **goods** (cars, furniture, apparel, appliances) from **services** (medical care, insurance, transportation services, recreation, and shelter).
segments.tr: कोर के भीतर, अर्थशास्त्री अक्सर **सामान** (कार, फर्नीचर, परिधान, उपकरण) को **सेवाओं** (चिकित्सा देखभाल, बीमा, परिवहन सेवाएं, मनोरंजन और आवास) से अलग करते हैं।

segments.src: Goods prices respond strongly to supply chains and tariffs, while services tend to be tied to wages and move more slowly.
segments.tr: माल की कीमतें आपूर्ति श्रृंखलाओं और शुعار का कड़ाई से जवाब देती हैं, जबकि सेवाएं मजदूरी से जुड़ी होती हैं और अधिक धीरे-धीरे चलती हैं।

segments.src: A report in which "supercore" services (core services excluding housing) stays elevated may signal different pressures than one driven by goods.
segments.tr: एक रिपोर्ट जिसमें "सुपरकोर" सेवाएं (आवास को छोड़कर कोर सेवाएं) ऊंची रहती हैं, माल द्वारा संचालित रिपोर्ट की तुलना में विभिन्न दबावों का संकेत दे सकती हैं।

segments.src: ## How to Read the Report in Five Steps
segments.tr: ## पांच चरणों में रिपोर्ट कैसे पढ़ें

segments.src: 1. **Check the monthly change first.** The monthly figure, seasonally adjusted, shows the latest momentum. The annual (year-over-year) figure covers twelve months and can be influenced by what happened a year ago, a quirk known as the *base effect*.
segments.tr: 1. **पहले मासिक परिवर्तन की जाँच करें।** मौसमी रूप से समायोजित मासिक आंकड़ा नवीनतम गति दिखाता है। वार्षिक (साल-दर-साल) आंकड़ा बारह महीनों को कवर करता है और एक वर्ष पहले क्या हुआ था, से प्रभावित हो सकता है, जिसे *बेस इफेक्ट* के रूप में जाना जाता है।

segments.src: 2. **Compare headline and core.** A wide gap usually points to food or energy as the cause.
segments.tr: 2. **हेडलाइन और कोर की तुलना करें।** एक चौड़ा अंतर आमतौर पर कारण के रूप में भोजन या ऊर्जा की ओर इशारा करता है।

segments.src: 3. **Look at shelter.** Is it rising or easing, and how much of the core change does it explain?
segments.tr: 3. **आवास को देखें।** क्या यह बढ़ रहा है या कम हो रहा है, और यह कोर परिवर्तन का कितना हिस्सा बताता है?

segments.src: 4. **Look beyond the headline.** Goods, services excluding shelter, and categories you personally buy tell you more than a single number.
segments.tr: 4. **हेडलाइन से आगे देखें।** सामान, आवास को छोड़कर सेवाएं, और आपके द्वारा व्यक्तिगत रूप से खरीदी जाने वाली श्रेणियां आपको एक नंबर से अधिक बताती हैं।

segments.src: 5. **Compare with expectations.** Markets react to the gap between the reported figure and forecasts, not just the figure itself. A "hot" or "cool" label usually means above or below the consensus estimate, and the numbers are often revised or rounded in ways that make small misses look bigger than they are.
segments.tr: 5. **अपेक्षित परिणामों से तुलना करें।** बाजार रिपोर्ट किए गए आंकड़े और पूर्वानुमानों के बीच के अंतर पर प्रतिक्रिया करते हैं, न कि केवल आंकड़े पर। "गर्म" या "ठंडा" लेबल का मतलब आम तौर पर आम सहमति के अनुमान से ऊपर या नीचे होता है, और संख्या को अक्सर ऐसे तरीकों से संशोधित या गोल किया जाता है जो छोटी चूकों को उनसे बड़े लगते हैं।

segments.src: For a smoother view, some analysts follow alternative measures such as the Cleveland Fed's median and trimmed-mean CPI, which reduce the influence of extreme price moves.
segments.tr: एक सुचारू दृश्य के लिए, कुछ विश्लेषक क्लीवलैंड फेड के माध्य और ट्रिम किए गए-माध्य सीपीआई जैसे वैकल्पिक उपायों का पालन करते हैं, जो अत्यधिक मूल्य चालों के प्रभाव को कम करते हैं।

segments.src: ## Why the Official Number Can Miss What You Pay
segments.tr: ## आधिकारिक संख्या आपके भुगतान को क्यों मिस कर सकती है

segments.src: Even a well-built index describes an average that no real household matches exactly.
segments.tr: यहां तक कि एक अच्छी तरह से निर्मित सूचकांक एक औसत का वर्णन करता है जो कोई वास्तविक परिवार बिल्कुल मेल नहीं खाता है।

segments.src: Several reasons explain the mismatch:
segments.tr: कई कारण बेमेल बताते हैं:

segments.src: - **Your basket is different.** The CPI weights categories by typical spending. If you commute long distances, have young children, pay for private insurance, or rent in a fast-moving market, your mix may lean toward faster-rising items.
segments.tr: - **आपकी टोकरी अलग है।** सीपीआई विशिष्ट खर्च द्वारा श्रेणियों का वजन करता है। यदि आप लंबी दूरी तय करते हैं, छोटे बच्चे हैं, निजी बीमा के लिए भुगतान करते हैं, या तेजी से बढ़ते बाजार में किराए पर लेते हैं, तो आपका मिश्रण तेजी से बढ़ती वस्तुओं की ओर झुक सकता है।

segments.src: - **Prices vs. inflation.** Inflation is a rate of change. When inflation slows from, say, a high rate to a lower one, prices are still rising, just more slowly. Price *levels* generally do not fall back, so everyday costs can still feel high long after the annual rate has eased.
segments.tr: - **कीमतें बनाम मुद्रास्फीति।** मुद्रास्फीति परिवर्तन की दर है। जब मुद्रास्फीति धीमी हो जाती है, मान लीजिए, उच्च दर से कम दर पर, कीमतें अभी भी बढ़ रही हैं, बस अधिक धीरे-धीरे। मूल्य *स्तर* आम तौर पर वापस नहीं आते हैं, इसलिए वार्षिक दर कम होने के लंबे समय बाद भी दैनिक लागत उच्च महसूस हो सकती है।

segments.src: - **Frequent purchases loom larger.** People notice gas, eggs, and coffee more than they notice the price of a washing machine bought once every ten years. Frequent, visible purchases shape perception more than their budget share would suggest.
segments.tr: - **बार-बार खरीदारी बड़ी होती है।** लोग हर दस साल में एक बार खरीदी जाने वाली वाशिंग मशीन की कीमत की तुलना में गैस, अंडे और कॉफी को अधिक देखते हैं। लगातार, दृश्यमान खरीदारी उनके बजट हिस्से की तुलना में धारणा को अधिक आकार देती है।

segments.src: - **Quality adjustments.** The BLS adjusts prices when product quality changes, such as a phone with a better camera. This is intended to separate pure price changes from improvements, but consumers may not feel they are getting the extra value.
segments.tr: - **गुणवत्ता समायोजन।** बेहतर कैमरे वाले फोन जैसे उत्पाद की गुणवत्ता में बदलाव होने पर बीएलएस कीमतों को समायोजित करता है। इसका उद्देश्य शुद्ध मूल्य परिवर्तनों को सुधारों से अलग करना है, लेकिन उपभोक्ताओं को यह महसूस नहीं हो सकता है कि उन्हें अतिरिक्त मूल्य मिल रहा है।

segments.src: - **Shrinkflation and substitution.** Smaller packages at the same price are captured in the unit-price data, but the index also assumes consumers shift to alternatives when relative prices change. Not everyone can or wants to switch.
segments.tr: - **सिकुड़न और प्रतिस्थापन।** एक ही कीमत पर छोटे पैकेजों को यूनिट-मूल्य डेटा में कैप्चर किया जाता है, लेकिन सूचकांक यह भी मानता है कि सापेक्ष कीमतें बदलने पर उपभोक्ता विकल्पों पर स्थानांतरित हो जाते हैं। हर कोई स्विच नहीं कर सकता है या नहीं चाहता है।

segments.src: - **Regional differences.** National averages mask local conditions. Housing, utilities, and insurance costs vary widely by metro area.
segments.tr: - **क्षेत्रीय अंतर।** राष्ट्रीय औसत स्थानीय स्थिति को छुपाते हैं। आवास, उपयोगिताओं और बीमा लागत मेट्रो क्षेत्र द्वारा व्यापक रूप से भिन्न होती हैं।

segments.src: - **Income and wage timing.** If your pay rises slower than prices, you feel the squeeze regardless of what the index says; if it rises faster, the squeeze may feel milder.
segments.tr: - **आय और वेतन समय।** यदि आपका वेतन कीमतों की तुलना में धीमी गति से बढ़ता है, तो सूचकांक जो भी कहता है, उसकी परवाह किए बिना आपको निचोड़ महसूस होता है; यदि यह तेजी से बढ़ता है, तो निचोड़ हल्का महसूस हो सकता है।

segments.src: ## A Practical Way to Build Your Own Inflation Read
segments.tr: ## अपना खुद का मुद्रास्फीति पठन बनाने का एक व्यावहारिक तरीका

segments.src: - List your top spending categories and what you paid for each over the past year.
segments.tr: - अपनी शीर्ष खर्च श्रेणियों को सूचीबद्ध करें और पिछले वर्ष के दौरान प्रत्येक के लिए आपने क्या भुगतान किया।

segments.src: - Compare those with the matching CPI components, which the BLS publishes in detail, including regional tables.
segments.tr: - उनकी तुलना मिलान सीपीआई घटकों के साथ करें, जिसे बीएलएस क्षेत्रीय तालिकाओं सहित विस्तार से प्रकाशित करता है।

segments.src: - Note which costs are fixed (a fixed-rate mortgage, a locked lease) and which are exposed (groceries, fuel, insurance renewals).
segments.tr: - ध्यान दें कि कौन सी लागत निश्चित हैं (एक निश्चित-दर बंधक, एक बंद पट्टा) और कौन सी उजागर हैं (किराना, ईंधन, बीमा नवीनीकरण)।

segments.src: - Use the result for budgeting and for conversations about pay, rather than relying on a single national percentage.
segments.tr: - एकल राष्ट्रीय प्रतिशत पर भरोसा करने के बजाय, बजट और वेतन के बारे में बातचीत के लिए परिणाम का उपयोग करें।

segments.src: ## The Bottom Line
segments.tr: ## निचला रेखा

segments.src: The CPI is a valuable, carefully constructed tool, but it is an average of a basket, not a bill of your own.
segments.tr: - **हेडलाइन मुद्रास्फीति आपको बताती है कि पूरी टोकरी कितनी चली गई; कोर मुद्रास्फीति आपको यह देखने में मदद करती है कि अंतर्निहित दबाव कितना लगातार है; और आवास, भोजन और ऊर्जा प्रत्येक कहानी का एक अलग हिस्सा बताते हैं।**

segments.src: Headline inflation tells you how much the full basket moved; core inflation helps you see how persistent the underlying pressure is; and shelter, food, and energy each tell a different part of the story.
segments.tr: हेडलाइन मुद्रास्फीति आपको बताती है कि पूरी टोकरी कितनी चली गई; कोर मुद्रास्फीति आपको यह देखने में मदद करती है कि अंतर्निहित दबाव कितना लगातार है; और आवास, भोजन और ऊर्जा प्रत्येक कहानी का एक अलग हिस्सा बताते हैं।

segments.src: Reading the next report with those distinctions in mind will help you separate noise from trend, and explain why the data and your wallet sometimes seem to disagree.
segments.tr: उन भेदों को ध्यान में रखते हुए अगली रिपोर्ट पढ़ना आपको प्रवृत्ति से शोर को अलग करने में मदद करेगा, और समझाएगा कि डेटा और आपका बटुआ कभी-कभी असहमत क्यों प्रतीत होता है।

es.title: Titular frente a subyacente: Cómo leer el próximo informe del IPC y por qué sus precios se sienten diferentes

segments.src: Once a month, usually at 8:30 a.m.
segments.tr: Una vez al mes, generalmente a las 8:30 a.m.

segments.src: Eastern on a weekday around the middle of the month, the U.S.
segments.tr: hora del Este en un día laborable alrededor de mediados de mes, la Oficina de Estadísticas Laborales (BLS) de EE. UU.

segments.src: Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) publishes the Consumer Price Index (CPI).
segments.tr: publica el Índice de Precios al Consumidor (IPC).

segments.src: Within minutes, headlines announce whether inflation "cooled," "reheated," or "surprised."
segments.tr: En cuestión de minutos, los titulares anuncian si la inflación "se enfrió", "se recalentó" o "sorprendió".

segments.src: Yet many readers look at their own grocery receipts, rent, and gas bills and wonder why the official number doesn't match their experience.
segments.tr: Sin embargo, muchos lectores miran sus propios recibos de supermercado, alquiler y facturas de gas y se preguntan por qué la cifra oficial no coincide con su experiencia.

segments.src: This guide explains what the CPI measures, how the headline and core readings differ, what each major category contributes, and why your personal inflation rate can differ from the national figure.
segments.tr: Esta guía explica qué mide el IPC, en qué se diferencian las lecturas del titular y la subyacente, qué aporta cada categoría principal y por qué su tasa de inflación personal puede diferir de la cifra nacional.

segments.src: It is educational background, not financial advice.
segments.tr: Es un contexto educativo, no un consejo financiero.

segments.src: ## Why the CPI Matters
segments.tr: ## Por qué importa el IPC

segments.src: The CPI tracks the average change over time in prices paid by urban consumers for a fixed basket of goods and services.
segments.tr: El IPC rastrea el cambio promedio a lo largo del tiempo en los precios pagados por los consumidores urbanos por una cesta fija de bienes y servicios.

segments.src: It feeds into several things that touch daily life:
segments.tr: Alimenta varias cosas que afectan la vida diaria:

segments.src: - **Interest-rate expectations.** The Federal Reserve targets 2% inflation, measured by a related gauge called the PCE price index. Markets still treat the CPI, which arrives earlier, as a key signal for where rates may go. Rates, in turn, influence mortgages, car loans, credit cards, and savings yields.
segments.tr: - **Expectativas de tipos de interés.** La Reserva Federal apunta a una inflación del 2%, medida por un indicador relacionado llamado índice de precios PCE. Los mercados todavía tratan al IPC, que llega antes, como una señal clave de hacia dónde pueden ir los tipos. Los tipos, a su vez, influyen en hipotecas, préstamos para automóviles, tarjetas de crédito y rendimientos de ahorro.

segments.src: - **Social Security cost-of-living adjustments (COLAs).** The annual COLA is based on the CPI-W, a variant covering urban wage earners and clerical workers. It compares the third-quarter average with the prior year's third quarter.
segments.tr: - **Ajustes por costo de vida (COLA) del Seguro Social.** El COLA anual se basa en el IPC-W, una variante que cubre a los asalariados urbanos y trabajadores administrativos. Compara el promedio del tercer trimestre con el tercer trimestre del año anterior.

segments.src: - **Wages and contracts.** Some labor agreements, leases, and benefit programs reference CPI changes, and inflation figures shape wage negotiations.
segments.tr: - **Salarios y contratos.** Algunos acuerdos laborales, contratos de arrendamiento y programas de beneficios hacen referencia a los cambios del IPC, y las cifras de inflación dan forma a las negociaciones salariales.

segments.src: - **Tax and program parameters.** Federal income tax brackets and certain benefit thresholds are adjusted each year using a CPI-based measure.
segments.tr: - **Parámetros fiscales y de programas.** Los tramos del impuesto federal sobre la renta y ciertos umbrales de beneficios se ajustan cada año utilizando una medida basada en el IPC.

segments.src: ## Headline vs. Core: What's the Difference?
segments.tr: ## Titular frente a subyacente: ¿Cuál es la diferencia?

segments.src: **Headline CPI** covers everything in the basket.
segments.tr: El **IPC titular** cubre todo lo que hay en la cesta.

segments.src: **Core CPI** removes food and energy.
segments.tr: El **IPC subyacente** elimina los alimentos y la energía.

segments.src: Those two categories tend to swing sharply because of weather, crop conditions, geopolitical events, and oil-market shifts.
segments.tr: Esas dos categorías tienden a oscilar bruscamente debido al clima, las condiciones de los cultivos, los eventos geopolíticos y los cambios en el mercado del petróleo.

segments.src: Stripping them out can give a steadier read on underlying trends, which is why many economists and policymakers watch core closely.
segments.tr: Eliminarlas puede dar una lectura más estable de las tendencias subyacentes, razón por la cual muchos economistas y responsables de políticas observan de cerca la subyacente.

segments.src: Core is not "the real inflation" and headline is not "the fake one."
segments.tr: La subyacente no es "la inflación real" y la titular no es "la falsa".

segments.src: They answer different questions:
segments.tr: Responden a preguntas diferentes:

segments.src: - Headline asks: *How much more does the typical household's total spending cost?*
segments.tr: - El titular pregunta: *¿Cuánto más cuesta el gasto total del hogar típico?*

segments.src: - Core asks: *Is price pressure broadening and persisting beyond volatile items?*
segments.tr: - La subyacente pregunta: *¿La presión sobre los precios se está ampliando y persistiendo más allá de los artículos volátiles?*

segments.src: Food and energy are not optional for most families, so a core reading that looks calm can sit alongside a headline reading that feels painful, and the reverse can also happen.
segments.tr: Los alimentos y la energía no son opcionales para la mayoría de las familias, por lo que una lectura subyacente que parece tranquila puede coexistir con una lectura titular que se siente dolorosa, y lo inverso también puede ocurrir.

segments.src: ## The Big Components, One by One
segments.tr: ## Los grandes componentes, uno por uno

segments.src: ### Shelter
segments.tr: ### Vivienda

segments.src: Shelter is the largest piece of the index, typically around one-third of the overall CPI and a larger share of core.
segments.tr: La vivienda es la parte más grande del índice, típicamente alrededor de un tercio del IPC general y una mayor parte de la subyacente.

segments.src: It includes rent of primary residences and "owners' equivalent rent" (OER), which estimates what homeowners would pay to rent their own homes.
segments.tr: Incluye el alquiler de residencias principales y el "alquiler equivalente de los propietarios" (OER), que estima lo que los propietarios pagarían por alquilar sus propias casas.

segments.src: It does not directly track home purchase prices or mortgage payments.
segments.tr: No rastrea directamente los precios de compra de viviendas ni los pagos de hipotecas.

segments.src: Two features matter when reading the report:
segments.tr: Dos características importan al leer el informe:

segments.src: 1. **Lag.** Rent data are collected from a rotating sample, with each housing unit surveyed only periodically. As a result, the CPI can reflect changes in new-lease market rents months after private rent trackers show them.
segments.tr: 1. **Retraso.** Los datos de alquiler se recopilan de una muestra rotativa, y cada unidad de vivienda se encuesta solo periódicamente. Como resultado, el IPC puede reflejar cambios en los alquileres del mercado de nuevos contratos meses después de que los rastreadores de alquiler privados los muestren.

segments.src: 2. **Weight.** Because shelter is so big, a small monthly change can move core CPI noticeably.
segments.tr: 2. **Peso.** Debido a que la vivienda es tan grande, un pequeño cambio mensual puede mover el IPC subyacente notablemente.

segments.src: If you rent, your experience may differ from the average, especially if your lease just renewed.
segments.tr: Si alquila, su experiencia puede diferir del promedio, especialmente si su contrato de arrendamiento acaba de renovarse.

segments.src: If you own a home with a fixed-rate mortgage, your housing payment may barely change even while the index's shelter component rises.
segments.tr: Si posee una casa con una hipoteca de tasa fija, su pago de vivienda puede apenas cambiar incluso mientras el componente de vivienda del índice aumenta.

segments.src: ### Food
segments.tr: ### Alimentos

segments.src: Food is split into "food at home" (groceries) and "food away from home" (restaurants and takeout).
segments.tr: Los alimentos se dividen en "alimentos en el hogar" (supermercado) y "alimentos fuera del hogar" (restaurantes y comida para llevar).

segments.src: Grocery prices can be volatile, driven by weather, animal disease, transportation costs, and global supply.
segments.tr: Los precios de los supermercados pueden ser volátiles, impulsados por el clima, enfermedades animales, costos de transporte y suministro global.

segments.src: Restaurant prices tend to move more steadily because they include labor and rent costs.
segments.tr: Los precios de los restaurantes tienden a moverse de manera más constante porque incluyen costos de mano de obra y alquiler.

segments.src: ### Energy
segments.tr: ### Energía

segments.src: Energy covers gasoline, electricity, natural gas, and fuel oil.
segments.tr: La energía cubre gasolina, electricidad, gas natural y combustible para calefacción.

segments.src: Gasoline often drives the largest month-to-month swings in headline inflation.
segments.tr: La gasolina a menudo impulsa las mayores oscilaciones mes a mes en la inflación titular.

segments.src: A drop at the pump can pull the headline number down even if nothing else has changed, and a spike can do the opposite.
segments.tr: Una caída en el surtidor puede reducir la cifra titular incluso si nada más ha cambiado, y un pico puede hacer lo contrario.

segments.src: ### Core goods and core services
segments.tr: ### Bienes subyacentes y servicios subyacentes

segments.src: Within core, economists often separate **goods** (cars, furniture, apparel, appliances) from **services** (medical care, insurance, transportation services, recreation, and shelter).
segments.tr: Dentro de la subyacente, los economistas a menudo separan los **bienes** (automóviles, muebles, ropa, electrodomésticos) de los **servicios** (atención médica, seguros, servicios de transporte, recreación y vivienda).

segments.src: Goods prices respond strongly to supply chains and tariffs, while services tend to be tied to wages and move more slowly.
segments.tr: Los precios de los bienes responden fuertemente a las cadenas de suministro y aranceles, mientras que los servicios tienden a estar vinculados a los salarios y se mueven más lentamente.

segments.src: A report in which "supercore" services (core services excluding housing) stays elevated may signal different pressures than one driven by goods.
segments.tr: Un informe en el que los servicios "supercore" (servicios subyacentes excluyendo vivienda) se mantienen elevados puede señalar presiones diferentes a uno impulsado por bienes.

segments.src: ## How to Read the Report in Five Steps
segments.tr: ## Cómo leer el informe en cinco pasos

segments.src: 1. **Check the monthly change first.** The monthly figure, seasonally adjusted, shows the latest momentum. The annual (year-over-year) figure covers twelve months and can be influenced by what happened a year ago, a quirk known as the *base effect*.
segments.tr: 1. **Verifique primero el cambio mensual.** La cifra mensual, ajustada estacionalmente, muestra el impulso más reciente. La cifra anual (año tras año) cubre doce meses y puede verse influenciada por lo que sucedió hace un año, una peculiaridad conocida como el *efecto base*.

segments.src: 2. **Compare headline and core.** A wide gap usually points to food or energy as the cause.
segments.tr: 2. **Compare el titular y el subyacente.** Una brecha amplia generalmente apunta a los alimentos o la energía como la causa.

segments.src: 3. **Look at shelter.** Is it rising or easing, and how much of the core change does it explain?
segments.tr: 3. **Mire la vivienda.** ¿Está subiendo o disminuyendo, y cuánto del cambio subyacente explica?

segments.src: 4. **Look beyond the headline.** Goods, services excluding shelter, and categories you personally buy tell you more than a single number.
segments.tr: 4. **Mire más allá del titular.** Los bienes, los servicios excluyendo la vivienda y las categorías que usted compra personalmente le dicen más que una sola cifra.

segments.src: 5. **Compare with expectations.** Markets react to the gap between the reported figure and forecasts, not just the figure itself. A "hot" or "cool" label usually means above or below the consensus estimate, and the numbers are often revised or rounded in ways that make small misses look bigger than they are.
segments.tr: 5. **Compare con las expectativas.** Los mercados reaccionan a la brecha entre la cifra reportada y los pronósticos, no solo a la cifra en sí. Una etiqueta de "caliente" o "frío" generalmente significa por encima o por debajo de la estimación de consenso, y los números a menudo se revisan o redondean de maneras que hacen que las pequeñas fallas parezcan más grandes de lo que son.

segments.src: For a smoother view, some analysts follow alternative measures such as the Cleveland Fed's median and trimmed-mean CPI, which reduce the influence of extreme price moves.
segments.tr: Para una visión más fluida, algunos analistas siguen medidas alternativas como el IPC de media y media recortada de la Fed de Cleveland, que reducen la influencia de los movimientos extremos de precios.

segments.src: ## Why the Official Number Can Miss What You Pay
segments.tr: ## Por qué la cifra oficial puede perderse lo que usted paga

segments.src: Even a well-built index describes an average that no real household matches exactly.
segments.tr: Incluso un índice bien construido describe un promedio que ningún hogar real coincide exactamente.

segments.src: Several reasons explain the mismatch:
segments.tr: Varias razones explican el desajuste:

segments.src: - **Your basket is different.** The CPI weights categories by typical spending. If you commute long distances, have young children, pay for private insurance, or rent in a fast-moving market, your mix may lean toward faster-rising items.
segments.tr: - **Su cesta es diferente.** El IPC pondera las categorías por el gasto típico. Si viaja largas distancias, tiene niños pequeños, paga un seguro privado o alquila en un mercado de rápido movimiento, su combinación puede inclinarse hacia artículos que aumentan más rápido.

segments.src: - **Prices vs. inflation.** Inflation is a rate of change. When inflation slows from, say, a high rate to a lower one, prices are still rising, just more slowly. Price *levels* generally do not fall back, so everyday costs can still feel high long after the annual rate has eased.
segments.tr: - **Precios frente a inflación.** La inflación es una tasa de cambio. Cuando la inflación se desacelera de, digamos, una tasa alta a una más baja, los precios siguen subiendo, solo que más lentamente. Los *niveles* de precios generalmente no caen, por lo que los costos diarios aún pueden sentirse altos mucho después de que la tasa anual se haya moderado.

segments.src: - **Frequent purchases loom larger.** People notice gas, eggs, and coffee more than they notice the price of a washing machine bought once every ten years. Frequent, visible purchases shape perception more than their budget share would suggest.
segments.tr: - **Las compras frecuentes cobran mayor importancia.** La gente nota la gasolina, los huevos y el café más de lo que nota el precio de una lavadora comprada una vez cada diez años. Las compras frecuentes y visibles moldean la percepción más de lo que sugeriría su participación en el presupuesto.

segments.src: - **Quality adjustments.** The BLS adjusts prices when product quality changes, such as a phone with a better camera. This is intended to separate pure price changes from improvements, but consumers may not feel they are getting the extra value.
segments.tr: - **Ajustes de calidad.** La BLS ajusta los precios cuando cambia la calidad del producto, como un teléfono con una mejor cámara. Esto tiene la intención de separar los cambios de precio puros de las mejoras, pero los consumidores pueden no sentir que están obteniendo el valor adicional.

segments.src: - **Shrinkflation and substitution.** Smaller packages at the same price are captured in the unit-price data, but the index also assumes consumers shift to alternatives when relative prices change. Not everyone can or wants to switch.
segments.tr: - **Reduflación y sustitución.** Los paquetes más pequeños al mismo precio se capturan en los datos de precio unitario, pero el índice también asume que los consumidores cambian a alternativas cuando cambian los precios relativos. No todos pueden o quieren cambiar.

segments.src: - **Regional differences.** National averages mask local conditions. Housing, utilities, and insurance costs vary widely by metro area.
segments.tr: - **Diferencias regionales.** Los promedios nacionales enmascaran las condiciones locales. Los costos de vivienda, servicios públicos y seguros varían ampliamente según el área metropolitana.

segments.src: - **Income and wage timing.** If your pay rises slower than prices, you feel the squeeze regardless of what the index says; if it rises faster, the squeeze may feel milder.
segments.tr: - **Momento de ingresos y salarios.** Si su salario aumenta más lento que los precios, siente la presión independientemente de lo que diga el índice; si aumenta más rápido, la presión puede sentirse más leve.

segments.src: ## A Practical Way to Build Your Own Inflation Read
segments.tr: ## Una forma práctica de construir su propia lectura de inflación

segments.src: - List your top spending categories and what you paid for each over the past year.
segments.tr: - Enumere sus principales categorías de gasto y lo que pagó por cada una durante el último año.

segments.src: - Compare those with the matching CPI components, which the BLS publishes in detail, including regional tables.
segments.tr: - Compárelas con los componentes del IPC correspondientes, que la BLS publica en detalle, incluidas las tablas regionales.

segments.src: - Note which costs are fixed (a fixed-rate mortgage, a locked lease) and which are exposed (groceries, fuel, insurance renewals).
segments.tr: - Tenga en cuenta qué costos son fijos (una hipoteca de tasa fija, un contrato de arrendamiento bloqueado) y cuáles están expuestos (supermercado, combustible, renovaciones de seguros).

segments.src: - Use the result for budgeting and for conversations about pay, rather than relying on a single national percentage.
segments.tr: - Use el resultado para presupuestar y para conversaciones sobre el salario, en lugar de depender de un solo porcentaje nacional.

segments.src: ## The Bottom Line
segments.tr: ## La conclusión

segments.src: The CPI is a valuable, carefully constructed tool, but it is an average of a basket, not a bill of your own.
segments.tr: El IPC es una herramienta valiosa y cuidadosamente construida, pero es un promedio de una cesta, no una factura propia.

segments.src: Headline inflation tells you how much the full basket moved; core inflation helps you see how persistent the underlying pressure is; and shelter, food, and energy each tell a different part of the story.
segments.tr: La inflación titular le dice cuánto se movió la cesta completa; la inflación subyacente le ayuda a ver cuán persistente es la presión subyacente; y la vivienda, los alimentos y la energía cuentan cada uno una parte diferente de la historia.

segments.src: Reading the next report with those distinctions in mind will help you separate noise from trend, and explain why the data and your wallet sometimes seem to disagree.
segments.tr: Leer el próximo informe con esas distinciones en mente le ayudará a separar el ruido de la tendencia, y explicar por qué los datos y su billetera a veces parecen no estar de acuerdo.
